surfaces.part: asphalt ground tile with crack, weeds and lane paint fragment

answer.evidence: The image is a flat 64x48 fully opaque ground texture of asphalt speckle with a dark crack, small green weeds and a yellow paint fragment. It has no front face, no edge line, no eave shadow and no silhouette change (width is 64 on every row). The darker horizontal rows in the column scan (e.g. rows 11, 15, 27, 31, 43, 47) are a repeating tile or texture pattern, not a vertical face. As a terrain tile it reads as flat ground seen from above.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a mid-grey asphalt field with only about 4 visible tones per tile and 15 distinct colours in total. The paving reference shows 7 tones with stones shaded one by one, and the grass reference has richer clumps. The grey ground has only faint speckle and no per-patch shading. Measured flat coverage is 0%, so there are no true flat fills, but the surface is uniform, low-contrast noise. The requested long crack is not visible as a continuous feature. Instead, one small crack-and-weed motif is stamped identically in each tile, which looks like a repeated sticker rather than a hand-shaded ground patch. The weed and paint bits are tiny, with only a yellow-green dab and a dark stroke and little shading depth. Only 27% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark marks lean tinted and the outline reads as mixed. Overall the piece is cleaner than flat but clearly shallower and less varied than the paving reference, so it does not hold up next to it.
